mainTopic: Workers treated as already warned, how much a departing planter is paid for his improvement, and whether the wood of an aged mortgaged orchard counts as produce or principal.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of workers who pay for damage they cause even without a warning. It then gives the general rule: any loss that cannot be undone counts as if they were warned. Next comes a story about a שתלא who wanted to leave for ארץ ישראל and asked to be paid for his improvement to the field. רבא pushes back twice, and רב פפא בר שמואל lowers the payment from the whole improvement, to half, to 'a quarter.' רב אשי explains that this 'quarter' is really a sixth of the whole, because only a sixth fits רב מניומי's rule that the owner must suffer no loss. רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף objects that the planter should not lose because the owner must pay a new אריס, and רב אשי praises the question without answering it. The גמרא then quotes more rulings of רב מניומי about the planter's share. Finally, a new case comes up: a mortgaged orchard that grew old. אביי says its wood is פירות and רבא says it is קרן. A ברייתא brought to challenge אביי is pushed aside, and the גמרא begins a new proof from a משנה about old vines that a married woman inherits.

steps.title: The town scribe is also treated as already warned
steps.stepSummary: The last item on a list of workers who are treated as already warned is the town scribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the town scribe: all of these workers are treated as if they were already warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the previous lines. It adds the town scribe to the workers who are treated as already warned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'treated as already warned' means these workers can be made to pay for a loss they cause, even if nobody warned them first. The town scribe writes documents for people, so a mistake by him can cause real harm.

keyTerms.meaning: The town scribe, who writes documents for the townspeople
As if already warned; they can be made to pay for a loss with no warning beforehand

phrases.english: and the town scribe —
all of them are considered as already warned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a list that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The town scribe, like the other workers on the list, is treated as already warned and pays for losses he causes.

steps.title: General rule: a loss that cannot be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the list with one principle: whenever the loss cannot be fixed, the worker is treated as already warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general rule is this: for any loss that cannot be undone, the worker is treated as already warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one rule that explains every case on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each worker on the list causes a kind of damage that cannot be fixed afterward. That is why no warning is needed before he has to pay. The rule turns a list of examples into one reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
That does not come back, that cannot be undone

steps.whatToRemember: Any loss that cannot be undone makes the worker liable, as if he had already been warned.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:
any loss that cannot be undone —
they are considered as already warned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the one principle behind the list in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any loss that cannot be undone makes the worker liable without a warning.

steps.title: A departing planter asks to be paid for his improvement
steps.stepSummary: A שתלא who wanted to move to ארץ ישראל asked to be paid for his work on the field, and רב פפא בר שמואל ruled that he should be paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a planter who told the field owners: 'Pay me for the improvement I made, because I want to go up to ארץ ישראל.' The case came before רב פפא בר שמואל, who told them: 'Pay him for his improvement.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. A planter wants to leave partway through his job and be paid for what he added to the field, and the first ruling is that he gets paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שתלא plants a field and normally earns a share of the produce over time. Here he wants to leave early and take the value of his improvement right now. רב פפא בר שמואל agrees, but he does not yet say how much the planter gets.

keyTerms.meaning: A planter who plants a field in exchange for a share of the produce
Improvement, the added value of the field
To go up to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: There was a certain planter who said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the owners of the field he was working on.

phrases.english: Give me my improvement
because I want to go up to the Land of Israel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: He came before Rav Pappa bar Shmuel.
He said to them: Give him his improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: paying a planter who leaves early.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא בר שמואל rules that the departing planter is paid for his improvement.

steps.title: רבא: the land also made the field better
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the planter should not get all the improvement, because the land itself helped produce it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Did the planter alone improve the field, and the land did nothing to improve it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the ruling. He says the planter cannot take credit for the whole improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added value came from two things working together: the planter's work and the owner's land. So paying the planter the full improvement gives him more than his part.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Did he improve it,
and the land did not improve it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִיהוּ אַשְׁבַּח, אַרְעָא לָא אַשְׁבַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling to give the planter his full improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The land helped create the improvement, so the planter does not deserve all of it.

steps.title: Only half of the improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל explains that he meant only half of the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am telling you that he gets half of the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל answers רבא by making his ruling clearer: the planter gets only half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the usual deal, where the planter and the owner each take half. Half goes to the planter for his work, and the land's half stays with the owner.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am telling you half of the improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the ruling more precise by lowering the amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The planter gets the full improvement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The planter gets half of the improvement.

steps.title: רבא: now the owner must also pay a sharecropper
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects again: once the planter leaves, the owner has to give a share to a new worker, so half is still too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Until now the owner took half and the planter took half. Now the owner has to give a share to a sharecropper!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the new amount. Paying half still leaves the owner worse off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the owner kept half and the planter did the work. After the planter leaves, the owner must hire an אריס to keep working the field, and the אריס takes a share. If the departing planter also takes half, the owner ends up with less than his normal half.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharecropper who works the field for a share of the produce

phrases.english: He said to him: Until now
the owner would take half
and the planter half.
Now he needs to give a share to a sharecropper!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד הָאִידָּנָא הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת פַּלְגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the half-improvement answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Paying the planter half of the improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner must now also pay an אריס, so giving the planter half leaves the owner with a loss.

steps.title: Only a quarter of the improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל lowers the amount again: the planter gets a quarter of the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am saying a quarter of the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל answers by cutting the amount in half again, down to 'a quarter.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower payment makes room for the share the new אריס will take. The word 'quarter' is not explained yet, and the next steps argue over what it means.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am saying a quarter of the improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's second objection in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the ruling more precise by lowering the amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The planter gets half of the improvement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The planter gets 'a quarter' of the improvement.
steps.whatToRemember: After two rounds with רבא, the payment comes down from all of the improvement, to half, to 'a quarter.'

steps.title: רב אשי: the 'quarter' is really a sixth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי thought that the 'quarter' really means a quarter of the owner's share, which comes to a sixth of the whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי wanted to say that the 'quarter' is a quarter that equals a sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a reading of the word 'quarter.' This step sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an אריס takes a third, the owner holds two-thirds. A quarter of that two-thirds is one-sixth of the whole, called a דנקא. So 'quarter' would mean a sixth of the full improvement, not a true quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, he wanted to say (often a view that may later be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: The word סבר signals that this is רב אשי's first thought. Do not assume it is the final ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi thought to say
"a quarter" that is a sixth.
phrases.notes: A quarter of the owner's two-thirds works out to one-sixth of the whole improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the 'quarter' in step 7 means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'A quarter' means a quarter of the owner's share, which is one-sixth of the whole.

steps.title: רב מניומי: the owner must not lose
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports his reading with רב מניומי's ruling: a departing planter is paid in a way that causes the owner no loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב מניומי the son of רב נחומי said: In a place where a planter takes half and a sharecropper takes a third, a planter who wants to leave is paid for his improvement and sent off in a way that the owner suffers no loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up רב אשי. It sets a rule: whatever the departing planter gets, the owner must not lose because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling describes the exact situation: planters take half and sharecroppers take a third. The planter's payment has to leave the owner with his usual half. That gives a clear test for how much the planter should get.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place, in a location

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets the test, 'no loss to the owner,' that decides how to read 'a quarter.'

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי:
phrases.english: As Rav Minyumi son of Rav Nechumi said:
In a place where a planter takes half
and a sharecropper a third,
this planter who wants to leave —
we give him the improvement and remove him

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נִמְטְיֵיהּ הֶפְסֵד לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: in a way that the owner will not suffer a loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב אשי's reading in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's reading that 'a quarter' means one-sixth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מניומי's ruling that a departing planter is paid in a way that causes the owner no loss.

steps.title: The math: only a sixth leaves the owner whole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a sixth leaves the owner with his half, while a true quarter would cost him half a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'a quarter' means a sixth, that works. But if you say it means a true quarter, the owner loses half of a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by doing the math. Only the 'sixth' reading fits רב מניומי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the אריס takes a third, the owner keeps two-thirds. Paying the planter a sixth leaves the owner with exactly half, so he loses nothing. Paying a true quarter leaves the owner with five-twelfths, which is half a sixth less than his half, and that breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the planter's 'quarter' is a sixth of the whole improvement, because only that amount keeps the owner from any loss.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
a quarter that is a sixth — fine,
but if you say an actual quarter,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מָטֵי לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: the owner suffers a loss
of half a sixth!
phrases.notes: Two-thirds minus a quarter leaves the owner five-twelfths instead of six-twelfths, so he is short one-twelfth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רִיבְעָא דְּהוּא דַּנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from step 9 to show that the reading in step 8 is right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'no loss to the owner' rule of רב מניומי, checked with numbers.

steps.title: Why should the planter lose for the sharecropper?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף challenges רב אשי: the planter can tell the owner to pay the new worker out of the owner's own half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב יוסף said to רב אשי: Let the planter say to the owner, 'You give your share to the sharecropper, and I will do whatever I want with my share.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא objects to רב אשי's idea that the planter only gets a sixth so that the owner loses nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי cut the planter's pay so that the owner would keep his full half after paying a new worker. רב אחא argues that the planter already did his half of the job. Hiring a new worker is the owner's business, so the planter should not lose because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: sharecropper, the new worker who takes over the field

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef said to Rav Ashi:
But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: Here the planter is speaking to the owner of the field.

phrases.aramaic: אַנְתְּ מְנָתָא דִּילָךְ – הַב לֵיהּ לַאֲרִיסָא,
phrases.english: You, your share, give it to the sharecropper,
and I, my share,
whatever I want, I will do with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רב אשי's sixth, which was just shown in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading that the planter gets only a sixth so the owner loses nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner's cost of hiring a new sharecropper should come out of his own half. It should not reduce the planter's earned half.

steps.title: רב אשי praises the question as a hard one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי does not answer. He tells רב אחא to bring this question to him when they learn the difficult מסכת זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When you get to 'Slaughter of קדשים', come and ask me this question.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי responds to the challenge by calling it a strong, sharp question, but he gives no actual answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reply is a compliment. The question is worthy of a hard מסכת like זבחים. The difficulty is left standing, and no resolution is given here.

keyTerms.meaning: the slaughter of sacrifices, meaning מסכת זבחים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רב אשי answering the question. He is praising it and leaving it unanswered.

phrases.english: He said: When you reach 'Slaughter of Sacrifices',
phrases.notes: This is מסכת זבחים, a famously difficult מסכת.

phrases.english: come and ask me this hard question.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מָטֵית לִשְׁחִיטַת קֳדָשִׁים, תָּא וְאַקְשִׁי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב אחא's challenge from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רב אשי would defend his sixth against רב אחא's objection
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No real answer. The question is praised as worthy of a hard מסכת and left standing.

steps.title: רב מניומי's full ruling on the departing planter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to quote רב מניומי's ruling in full: a departing planter is paid in a way that causes the owner no loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the ruling itself. רב מניומי son of רב נחומי said: In a place where the planter takes half and the sharecropper a third, if a planter wants to leave, we give him his share of the improvement and remove him, so that the owner does not lose.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to the ruling of רב מניומי that was quoted in step 9 as a proof. It now presents that ruling on its own, so it can add his other rulings about planters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling adds the local background. Planters take half and sharecroppers take a third. When the planter leaves, his payment is set up so that the owner still keeps his share after paying a sharecropper.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself', meaning going back to quote a statement in full
the planter who plants and develops a field
his improvement, the value he added

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Minyumi son of Rav Nechumi said:
In a place where the planter takes half
and the sharecropper a third,
this planter who wants to leave,
we give him his improvement and send him off,
phrases.notes: He means the planter's share of the improvement, not its whole value.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִיפְסוֹד בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: so that the owner should not lose.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the source that רב אשי cited in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A departing planter receives his share of the improvement, calculated so that the owner suffers no loss.

steps.title: Old vine gets half; flooded trees get a quarter
steps.stepSummary: רב מניומי adds two rulings: the planter gets half of an old vine, and a quarter when a river floods the vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מניומי son of רב נחומי also said: An old vine, the planter gets half. If a river washed it away, he gets a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two more rulings from the same אמורא about how much the planter receives in special cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The planter gets half even of a vine that was there before he came. When a flood knocks the trees down and the wood is divided, his share drops to a quarter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי:
phrases.english: Rav Minyumi son of Rav Nechumi said:
An old vine: half.
phrases.notes: This is a vine that was already there before the planter came, and he still gets half.

phrases.english: A river washed it away: a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי: קוֹפָא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further rulings from the same אמורא about the planter's share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The planter takes half of an old vine and a quarter of trees knocked down by a flood.
steps.whatToRemember: The planter section ends here. רב אשי sets the departing planter's pay at a sixth so the owner loses nothing, but רב אחא's challenge to that is left unanswered.

steps.title: Mortgaged orchard grows old: אביי says the wood is produce
steps.stepSummary: A man gave an orchard as a משכנתא for ten years, and it aged after five. אביי rules that the wood is פירות, so the lender may take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man mortgaged an orchard to his friend for ten years, and it grew old after five years. אביי said: It is produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a real case. אביי gives the first opinion on who owns the wood of an orchard that became too old to bear fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under a משכנתא, the lender eats the fruit but does not own the land itself. When the trees grow old and are only good for wood, אביי treats that wood like fruit, so it belongs to the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: mortgaged, gave as a pledge whose fruit the lender eats

phrases.english: A certain man mortgaged an orchard to his friend
for ten years, and it grew old after five years.
Abaye said: It is produce.
phrases.notes: He means the wood of the old trees, which can now only be cut down and sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new sugya about a משכנתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the wood of trees that aged during the משכנתא counts as פירות and belongs to the lender.

steps.title: רבא says the wood is principal
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: the wood is קרן. Land is bought with the money from it, and the lender eats that land's fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is principal. Land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposing opinion in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the trees are part of the field itself, and the lender never owned the field. So the wood money buys new land, and the lender eats that land's fruit for the rest of the term.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is principal,

phrases.aramaic: וְיִלָּקַח בּוֹ קַרְקַע, וְהוּא אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: and land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender, who eats the fruit of the new land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: the wood is קרן. Land is bought with its value, and the lender eats that land's fruit.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a dried or cut tree is sold to buy land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets up a challenge to אביי: when a mortgaged tree dries up or is cut down, it is sold and land is bought with the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If the tree dried up or was cut down, both are forbidden to use it. What should they do? It is sold for wood, land is bought with the money, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge אביי. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא handles the wood the way רבא does. It is sold, land is bought, and the lender eats only that land's fruit. The open question is whether this ברייתא really matches our case of an orchard that aged in its normal time.

phrases.english: They challenged: If the tree dried up or was cut down,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a field given as a משכנתא.

phrases.english: both are forbidden to use it.
phrases.notes: 'Both' means the lender and the borrower; neither may take the wood for himself.

phrases.english: What should they do? They are sold for wood,

phrases.aramaic: וְיִלָּקַח בָּהֶן קַרְקַע, וְהוּא אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת.
phrases.english: and land is bought with the money, and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the dispute between אביי and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that the wood is פירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the wood of a dead tree as קרן, which matches רבא's ruling.

steps.title: Drying up in its time means the wood is principal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'dried up' as being like 'cut down', meaning a tree that ended at its proper time. So the ברייתא proves the wood is קרן, against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't 'dried up' like 'cut down'? Just as cut down means at its proper time, so too dried up means at its proper time. And it teaches that land is bought with it and he eats the produce. So it is principal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא applies to our case and concludes that it supports רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dried up' is listed next to 'cut down', so both are read as describing a tree that ended in its normal time, just like our orchard that naturally grew old. Since even then the ברייתא says to buy land, the wood is קרן. That is רבא's view and a challenge to אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it so that...? (opening a proof)

phrases.english: Is it not that 'dried up' is like 'cut down':

phrases.aramaic: מָה נִקְצַץ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, אַף יָבַשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ,
phrases.english: just as cut down is at its proper time, so too dried up is at its proper time,
and it teaches: land is bought with them
and he eats the produce.
Apparently, it is principal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 17 by reading the ברייתא as matching our case.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the wood is קרן, and against אביי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a tree that dried up or was cut down, read as ending at its proper time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a tree that ended naturally is treated as קרן, so the wood cannot be פירות.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא, read as 'dried up in its proper time', supports רבא that the wood of an aged orchard is קרן. That leaves a difficulty for אביי.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about trees lost before their time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof against אביי. 'Cut down' should be read like 'dried up': both mean the tree ended early and unexpectedly. So the ברייתא does not speak about אביי's case of an orchard that aged naturally.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Cut down' is like 'dried up'. Just as 'dried up' means it dried up before its time, so too 'cut down' means it was cut down before its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the earlier reading around to defend אביי. Instead of reading 'dried up' like 'cut down', it reads 'cut down' like 'dried up', and both mean an early, unexpected loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the proof against אביי depended on the ברייתא talking about trees that ended at their proper time. Now the גמרא says the ברייתא is about trees that ended early. That kind of sudden loss is different from אביי's case, where the orchard simply grew old as trees normally do, so the ברייתא does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: No. The word that opens a rejection of the previous argument
Before its time, earlier than expected

steps.confusionAlert: Both Step 18 and this step compare 'dried up' and 'cut down'. They just go in opposite directions. Step 18 read both as ending at the right time. Here both are read as ending too early.

phrases.english: No:
'cut down' is similar to 'dried up';
phrases.notes: This flips the comparison from Step 18. There 'dried up' was read like 'cut down'.

phrases.english: just as 'dried up' is before its time,
so too 'cut down' is before its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 18 by reading the ברייתא in the opposite direction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא against אביי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא spoke of trees that ended at their proper time. It can be read as talking about trees lost early, which is not אביי's case.

steps.title: A new proof attempt from old vines a woman inherits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new proof, quoting a משנה about old vines and olive trees that come to a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if old vines and olive trees came to her (by inheritance)...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts quoting a משנה to bring a new proof, and the main point comes in the next part of the quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a married woman whose property is used by her husband, who may eat the produce but not use up the main property. Old trees that stop giving fruit raise the same question as our case: is the wood like fruit or like the main property? The answer will be used to decide between אביי and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to her, usually by inheritance

phrases.english: Come and hear:
if old vines and olive trees came to her,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is a married woman. This is a משנה from כתובות 79b.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נָפְלוּ לָהּ גְּפָנִים וְזֵיתִים זְקֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was pushed away, the גמרא tries a new source to settle the argument.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the wood of trees that aged is קרן, as רבא says
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כתובות about old vines and olive trees that a married woman inherits
